chapter: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
title: Summer pops concerts in Congo Square
summary: He played the summer pops for many years, rehearsing mornings and performing at night at Congo Square, and enjoyed it.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, mostly we were all symphony fellas. And of course there would be a lot of fellas that came in and only played one number and that was it, you know. And we got paid for two. It was very remarkable that a thing like that would start Xavier University, you know. Somebody had to start it, had to be somewhere, and that was it. It goes to show you what a swinging university that is. Did you ever work with the summer pops? Oh yes. Sure, I worked many years with the summer pops. Yeah. We used to be out there and rehearse in the morning and the scorching sunlight out in the, what is it, what's the name of that square? Congo Square. Congo Square. Congo Square, yeah. They don't call it Congo Square now, do they?
Call it Boriga. But some people call it Congo Square. Boriga. They still call it Congo Square? Some of them do.

They still call it. They still call it the night. I, well anyway, the stage was set up over there and we'd rehearse every morning over there and then play the concerts at night. I enjoyed playing the pops very much. I think New Orleans enjoyed having it too. You can tell by the attendance. And, uh. My dear boy, what are you doing?
